# Lucent · 灵感台

> An inspiration launcher. Lucent is a calm personal base that a working day starts from and every search lifts off from — and, when you would rather go nowhere, a place still worth staying in. Designed by hydeclanspi for a Huawei MatePad Edge (14.2-inch 3:2 OLED, 3120×2080, laid out on 1560×1040 CSS pixels) as a custom homepage for the Aira browser on HarmonyOS; published here as a web edition (source in src/, demonstrations in showcase/). Vanilla HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas and SVG; no framework, no runtime dependency, no request to any other site after load. The web edition carries the MatePad's own typefaces — HarmonyOS Sans, and Noto Sans Mono for figures — sliced by scripts/web-fonts.py so a page loads only its core and a rare character fetches its own slice.

Narrative: there was once a button below the screen, and everyone called it the Home button — press it, and however far you had gone, you were back where you began. Home was a promise: there is always a place that waits for you. Lucent makes that promise into a place. (The product is named Lucent · 灵感台; "Home" refers only to the button and its promise.) Tagline: "Launch from here. Stay for the light." (由此出发，为光停留。) The 台 in its Chinese name 灵感台 is read four ways — a workbench, a launch pad, a stage and a console — and residents live on it. Design standard: 灵感与犀利并存 — inspired, and incisive.

Five parts:

- Workbench (the base): clock and greeting, profile, search with four engines, shortcuts in three forms and 28 colours, direct entries, a one-line note archived to the second; focus mode when both sections fold; a short-screen guard keeps the history tag clear of the top bar.
- Residents (alive): Lueurs, 49 numbered glass lenses in a hand-drawn 35-vertex region. Ornstein–Uhlenbeck heading with velocity relaxation; 4 px sub-stepped impulse physics (restitution 0.64, speed cap 640 px/s) with an eight-direction scattering score; Drive (FSD), a roam/chase/charge/coast state machine on a breadth-first navigation grid with line-of-sight simplification; natural encounters adjudicated at 70% inside a 150 px circle; desert-punishing weighted placement ("stones and constellations"); dragging moves an invisible potential field that sets the Light/Dark wallpaper odds. A chronicle keeps every resident's file, relationships, residency terrain and drive log in checksummed dual-slot snapshots with hour → day → month → year compaction and largest-remainder migration; backups use a self-verifying text format (AIRAPC1: deflate-raw, base64url, CRC-32, segmented).
- Launch pad: 念起，光行 (A thought, in flight) — the typed words become light that reaches the arrow before the search departs. Six motions chosen from a sixteen-study atelier; each Canvas renderer is a pure function of progress, so frames can be slowed to 0.35×, reversed and tested.
- Stage (loop): an endless simulated launch that sends no search — a first shot that flies back, bursts while Enter is held, one-bit demand — and Random mode's platinum conduits with blue-white lasers whose speeds are drawn from a truncated normal N(0.70, 0.10²) and whose waves never share a lane.
- Console (control): Lucent Glass with two finishes (Classic Frost, Warm Clear) and six 0–100 dials (clarity, softness, warmth, edge, colour, touch) for the card and the sheets separately, feeding six optical layers with no animation loop at rest; wallpaper soft focus, brightness and framing; Lueur count, strength, pace and odds; three layers of defaults. Every control has a second layer under a long press, with keyboard equivalents.

Made for one screen: the HUAWEI MatePad Edge. On a computer, the web edition's full screen is a faithful simulation of that screen — it goes full screen on the first click (F toggles), installs as an app that opens full screen, and draws the tablet's status bar, Aira's toolbar and the gesture bar at the device's sizes. Every visit opens on six Lueurs and a Random wallpaper at Light 99 : 1. Phones and small screens are outside its scope.

Concept film (showcase/film, published at /film/): 108 seconds with sound on one timeline — WebGL for the worlds (night, pearl, aurora, dawn), god rays, stage lights and four pillars of worlds; Canvas 2D for beams, lasers, the Home button seen as an arc, the world beyond a slit (a chip whose cores lift off as windows, then a tunnel of a thousand windows) and three wallpapers that arrive as panes of glass and drop into the MatePad's picker, two above and one below; CSS and SVG for the interface and type; WebGL points for glints and fireflies. render(t) is a pure function of time, so scripts/film.mjs renders it frame by frame to 1440p60 H.264 (2560 × 1440). Its score is synthesized with numpy by scripts/film-score.py from the same scene marks, on a grid of 120 beats a minute: a piano and a marimba with the tune, hands, a whistle and a ukulele beside them, strings, taiko and voices under every reveal, a four-on-the-floor only at the brightest moments; seven versions of it can be rendered (--list).

On-device recording (showcase/device, published at /device/): 54 seconds recorded on the HUAWEI MatePad Edge — a search and its Lightline, the search motions, the Lueurs' settings and history, the wallpapers, the card and the backup, then the gold silk and motes round the search field (5.1.3) and focus with both sections folded — edited by scripts/device-edit.py from two recordings: it opens on the README's cover, the quiet stretches run faster with their speed marked, and the music is the second half of the film's score. The page shows the cover and plays on a tap.

Verification: 41 unit tests (engine invariants such as momentum conservation, no tunnelling, a connected placement chamber, line-of-sight routes; renderer determinism over 21,618 progress states; storage integrity) and 22 browser flows run in CI. Documentation figures are drawn by the engine's own functions; screenshots, animations and the film are rendered frame by frame under a fake clock.

Evolution: 111 versions in 25 days (2.0.0 → 5.1.3). Product definition, design and sign-off by hydeclanspi; implementation written with AI coding agents.
